# Research: Client-View UI — Shared Itinerary (spec 010)

Phase 0 output. All Technical Context unknowns resolved. Decisions numbered D1–D11 and
referenced from plan.md / data-model.md / tasks.md.

## D1 — Share token: uuid v4 primary key, generated by Postgres

**Decision**: The share token IS the `itinerary_share_link` row's primary key: a
`uuid` column with `defaultRandom()` (Postgres `gen_random_uuid()`, cryptographically
strong since PG13). 122 bits of randomness satisfies FR-003 (≥120 bits, enumeration
infeasible).

**Rationale**: Zero new machinery — the platform already mints uuid PKs this way for
every product table; the token doubles as the row identity; Drizzle/zod `z.uuid()`
validation exists at every boundary.

**Alternatives considered**: (a) separate 256-bit hex token column — more entropy than
needed, second unique column, no product value at P0; (b) signed stateless tokens
(JWT-style) — unrevocable by design, contradicting the spec's "must not preclude
revocation later"; (c) app-side `crypto.randomUUID()` — equivalent entropy but moves
generation off the DB default used everywhere else.

## D2 — Redaction is an ALLOWLIST projection, in the api service layer

**Decision**: `toClientItineraryView(document, agencyName, bookedItemIds)` — a pure
function in `packages/api/src/services/client-view.ts` — builds the client payload by
**copying named safe fields only** (allowlist), never by deleting unsafe ones
(blocklist). Allowed: itinerary title + currency; day number/date; per item: kind,
title, kind-specific schedule facts (stay: checkIn/checkOut/occupancy; activity:
startsAt/durationMinutes; transfer: from/to/mode), `sellPrice.amountMinor`, booked
flag. Everything else — `netRate`, `supplyRef`, `provenance`, `pricing` block (budget
mode/total/categories), `tripRequest`, `agencyId`, item/doc ids, `media` (empty at v0)
— is structurally absent from the output type.

**Rationale**: For confidentiality, omission-by-construction beats deletion-by-
enumeration: a future schema field is confidential-by-default until someone explicitly
allowlists it. A blocklist silently leaks every field added after it was written.
Placing it in the service layer (the `itineraryOverview` precedent) keeps the router
thin and the function exhaustively unit-testable without a DB.

**Alternatives considered**: blocklist/`delete` on a document clone (rejected — leaks
future fields); redaction in the page component (rejected — the confidential values
would still cross the wire to the browser, failing SC-003's "payload, not pixels").

## D3 — Anonymous read = public tRPC procedure + server-side caller

**Decision**: New top-level `clientView` router on the app router:
`clientView.itinerary` is a `publicProcedure` taking `{ token: z.uuid() }` and
returning a typed union `{ status: "not_found" } | { status: "found"; view }`. The
`/view/[token]` **server component** invokes the same procedure through a server-side
caller (`appRouter.createCaller` over a null-session context built from the existing
container accessor in `apps/web/lib/trpc/server.ts`) — no self-HTTP hop.

**Rationale**: INV-018 — web and mobile consume one tRPC surface; the traveler client
view is exactly the kind of read the Expo app will need. A typed `not_found` value
(not a thrown error) matches the "friendly unavailable state, no existence oracle"
requirement (FR-003) and the repo's typed-business-failure convention. The server-side
caller keeps SSR fast while guaranteeing the page and any future mobile client share
one contract.

**Alternatives considered**: page reads the service directly (rejected — mobile would
need a parallel procedure later, and the page/API contracts could drift); page fetches
`/api/trpc` over HTTP (rejected — pointless self-roundtrip on the same process).

## D4 — Route shape: `/view/[token]` beside the existing `/view` placeholder

**Decision**: New dynamic segment `apps/web/app/(client-view)/view/[token]/page.tsx`.
The tokenless `/view` page is byte-untouched.

**Rationale**: `tests/e2e/trust-boundary.spec.ts` and `smoke.spec.ts` pin `/view`'s
exact behavior (heading, INV-020 negatives) — leaving it untouched keeps the sealed
regression surface green by construction. A path segment (vs `?token=` query) is
copy-paste friendly, works with `robots: noindex` metadata per page, and gives the
route group's layout full control of metadata inheritance (the iteration-2 [BUG-2]
lesson).

**Alternatives considered**: query param on `/view` (rejected — mutates the pinned
page's behavior matrix); a new top-level route outside `(client-view)` (rejected —
INV-024 puts all traveler surface in the client-view group).

## D5 — Share UI: minimal client component in the planner's drafted state

**Decision**: `<ShareControl itineraryId={...} />` composes into the planner's drafted
state next to `<BookingFlow>` (spec 009 precedent), calling
`workspace.itinerary.share` and rendering the returned path as an absolute URL
(`new URL(path, window.location.origin)`) with a copy-to-clipboard affordance. Pure
logic (URL join, transport-error mapping via the existing `transport-error.ts`) lives
in `apps/web/lib/share-control.ts` with L1 tests.

**Rationale**: The server returns a **path** (`/view/{token}`), not an absolute URL —
the serving origin is the browser's business (the BETTER_AUTH_URL/origin lesson from
seed-0009a T019: the server cannot know the canonical origin on alternate-port
boots). Reuses the established client-component + pure-lib pattern and the shared
transport-error strings.

**Alternatives considered**: server builds the absolute URL from env (rejected —
origin drift breaks alternate-port stacks and adds config); share affordance on a
separate itinerary list page (rejected — no such page exists yet; the drafted state is
where agents are).

## D6 — Booked marks come from `booking_component` rows

**Decision**: `resolveShareLink` reads the set of `item_id`s having a
`booking_component` row for the share's `(itinerary_id, agency_id)` and passes it to
the projection; items in the set render `booked: true`.

**Rationale**: `booking_component` rows exist only for CONFIRMED components (spec 005
FR-010) and carry item-level exclusivity (spec-gap-0002 unique index) — exactly the
"confirmed booking" semantics US3 needs. Quote/hold rows are agent-workspace concepts
(minutes-lived) and are deliberately not surfaced to travelers (spec Assumption).

**Alternatives considered**: joining `booking_quote` consumed rows (rejected —
consumption is a claim-gate mechanism, not a confirmation record); denormalizing a
`booked` flag into the document (rejected — would mutate the canonical document and
duplicate DB truth).

## D7 — No new PMF events

**Decision**: No `itinerary_shared` / view-count events in this feature.

**Rationale**: The PMF vocabulary is closed (`packages/db/src/pmf-events.ts`) and maps
to the constitution's mandated metrics (GBV, take-rate, resold ratio, plan→book);
share/view is none of them. Extension is additive-by-SDD when a metric needs it.

## D8 — Trip total: fold with domain `addMoney`, null when nothing is priced

**Decision**: The server computes `totalSellMinor` by folding priced items'
`sellPrice` through `packages/domain`'s `addMoney` (same-currency enforcement for
free); an itinerary with zero priced items gets `total: null` and the page omits the
total row.

**Rationale**: INV-010 (money math only in domain — reuse, not re-derive); the
canonical schema's single-currency refinement guarantees the fold is well-defined;
"€0.00 total" on an unpriced proposal would be a false price statement (FR-008 edge).

**Alternatives considered**: summing in the page (rejected — client-side money math,
FR-008); reusing `pricing.total` (rejected — that is the **budget** total, an
agent-confidential planning value, not the sell total).

## D9 — Share-link table: one durable link per itinerary, race-safe in the DB

**Decision**:

```
itinerary_share_link
  token        uuid PK default gen_random_uuid()
  agency_id    text NOT NULL → organization.id  (cascade)
  itinerary_id uuid NOT NULL UNIQUE → itinerary.id  (cascade)
  created_at   timestamp NOT NULL default now()
```

`createShareLink` = tenant-scoped itinerary ownership check (NOT_FOUND on
miss/cross-tenant, no oracle) → `INSERT … ON CONFLICT (itinerary_id) DO NOTHING` →
SELECT the (now-guaranteed) row. UNIQUE(itinerary_id) decides concurrent share races:
exactly one row survives, both callers receive the same token (FR-004/SC-006).

**Rationale**: The DB constraint is the arbiter (marketplace duplicate-license-gate
precedent, spec 006 FR-012) — no advisory locks, no app-level dedupe. `ON DELETE
CASCADE` from `itinerary` makes the deleted-itinerary edge case behave as unknown
token automatically. This is a DB schema addition, **not** a canonical itinerary
schema change (QS3-4 precedent: no version bump, no operator gate); the compose
`migrate` stage (`drizzle-kit push`) applies it.

**Alternatives considered**: many revocable links per itinerary (rejected — spec
scopes one durable link; the UNIQUE constraint is droppable later without data loss);
upsert-returning (rejected — `DO NOTHING` + select is the repo's established
read-after-conflict shape and avoids returning-clause dialect edge cases).

## D10 — Service placement: `packages/api/src/services/client-view.ts`

**Decision**: One new service module holding `createShareLink`, `resolveShareLink`,
and the pure `toClientItineraryView`, mirroring `services/booking.ts` /
`services/planner.ts`.

**Rationale**: This is app-surface behavior (share + anonymous read), not trade
(`packages/marketplace`) and not domain math (`packages/domain` — only `addMoney` is
consumed from there). The service layer is where tenancy-scoped DB access +
typed-outcome shapes already live.

## D11 — Page rendering: server component, `force-dynamic`, `robots: noindex`

**Decision**: `/view/[token]/page.tsx` is an async server component with
`export const dynamic = "force-dynamic"`; `generateMetadata` resolves the view (shared
per-request via React `cache()` around the resolve call) and emits an agency-branded
title (`"{trip title} — {agency name}"`), a neutral description, and
`robots: { index: false, follow: false }`. Invalid (non-uuid) tokens short-circuit to
the not-found state without touching the DB.

**Rationale**: Read-only content needs no client JS; `force-dynamic` prevents Next
from caching one traveler's private view or serving stale booked-state (the workspace
page precedent). `noindex` keeps unguessable links out of search indexes (FR-003
secrecy support). Metadata must be set at the page (not inherited platform metadata) —
the exact INV-020 leak class fixed in seed-0011.

**Alternatives considered**: client component + browser tRPC fetch (rejected — slower
first paint, leaks nothing extra but gains nothing); static generation (rejected —
private, per-token, must reflect current booked state).
